raw_response:
I am old now, 75 years, and alone in this house since my husband passed. Three mu is all I can manage, and even that is heavy work for me. I grow cotton like I always have — wheat and maize need too much bending and carrying, and cotton I can harvest slowly over many days by myself.

This year I will do what I did last year, because it worked. I finished with about 260 jin per mu of seed cotton, which is alright for my land. The soil here is decent but salty in patches, and cotton handles that better than grain.

For seed, I buy the Bt cotton seed from the dealer in town — the kind with the pest resistance built in. Everyone around here plants it now. Without it the bollworm eats you alive and you spray and spray. My neighbor's son told me about a new variety but I will stay with what I planted last year. At my age I don't experiment.

For fertilizer, I buy two bags of compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, before I plough. That is 100 jin, so about 33 jin per mu as base. Then when the cotton starts flowering, I put one bag of urea, 50 jin total, split across the field — mostly around bud stage and again when bolls are filling. I put a little more than the dealer says because if cotton is short of nitrogen the bolls stay small and I lose money. Fertilizer is cheaper than lost yield.

I plough before planting — I hire the tractor man from the village, 60 yuan per mu. I can't pull a plough myself and rotary doesn't work as well for cotton root here.

Irrigation from the well — I water before planting to get the seed up, again at bud stage, and once more when bolls are filling if no rain. So three times usually. The well water costs electricity but the cotton needs it.

Pesticide is the hard part. Even with Bt cotton, the aphids and spider mites and plant bugs still come. I spray maybe 6 times through the season. My nephew helps me with the sprayer because I cannot carry it anymore.
